prompts.label: Literal match basics
prompts.text:
Teach simplest regex literal matching for beginners.

- Match word cat in text with /cat/ or re.search
- Case sensitivity flag i
- Escape dots and special chars \.
- When substring indexOf enough instead

JavaScript and Python side-by-side one example each.

prompts.label: Character classes
prompts.text:
Explain character classes and shorthands.

- [aeiou], [0-9], negated [^0-9]
- \d \w \s and negated \D \W \S
- Match hex color # followed by six hex digits exercise

Provide test strings pass/fail table.

prompts.label: Anchors and word boundaries
prompts.text:
Demonstrate anchors and word boundaries.

- ^ start $ end of line/string (engine flags matter)
- \b word boundary vs \B
- Match whole word cat not catalog
- Multiline ^ per line mention

Examples with unexpected matches called out.

prompts.label: Quantifiers greedy and lazy
prompts.text:
Teach quantifiers with greedy vs lazy behavior.

- *, +, ?, {3}, {2,5}
- Greedy .* vs lazy .*? on HTML-like string caution
- When possessive quantifiers exist headline

Show one catastrophic overlap example visually in text.

prompts.label: Capturing groups
prompts.text:
Use capturing groups to extract parts.

- Pattern (\d{4})-(\d{2})-(\d{2}) for date
- Group 1 2 3 in replace or match object
- Non-capturing (?:...) when grouping only

JS match groups and Python .group(1).

prompts.label: Named capture groups
prompts.text:
Introduce named groups for readable extraction.

- JS (?<name>...) and Python (?P<name>...)
- Access via groups dict or match.groups
- Refactor numbered groups example to named

Same date parse using names year month day.

prompts.label: Alternation OR pattern
prompts.text:
Build alternation patterns carefully.

- (cat|dog|bird) matching one of
- Precedence trap: foo|food vs fo(o|od)
- Combine with character classes when simpler

List strings matching and non-matching.

prompts.label: Lookahead and lookbehind intro
prompts.text:
Explain lookaround assertions without consuming.

- Positive lookahead (?=\d{2}) for price ending
- Negative lookahead (?!...) password complexity teaser
- Lookbehind length limits in JS engine

One password must include digit example optional.

prompts.label: Replace with capture groups
prompts.text:
Transform text using regex replace and groups.

- Rename john.doe@email.com to Doe, John format
- JS replace with $1 $2 or callback
- Python re.sub with \1

Before/after string examples.

prompts.label: Validate email cautiously
prompts.text:
Show pragmatic email validation regex and its limits.

- Simple pattern [^@]+@[^@]+\.[^@]+
- Why full RFC email regex is impractical
- Prefer library validator in production
- HTML5 type=email and server-side double check

Discuss false positives/negatives honestly.

prompts.label: Parse log line exercise
prompts.text:
Write regex to parse log line into fields.

- Format: 2024-01-15T10:00:00 INFO User logged in id=42
- Extract timestamp, level, message, optional id
- Named groups recommended
- Test against three sample lines

Provide pattern and code reading groups.

prompts.label: Multiline and dotall flags
prompts.text:
Explain flags affecting ^ $ and dot.

- Multiline m: ^ matches line start
- Dotall s: dot matches newline
- JS /pattern/ms syntax
- Python re.MULTILINE | re.DOTALL

Parse multiline config file key=value example.

prompts.label: Catastrophic backtracking pitfalls
prompts.text:
Warn about catastrophic backtracking patterns.

- (a+)+b on aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaac
- Nested quantifiers danger
- Use atomic groups or possessive where supported
- Timeout or regex-safe libraries in servers

Show evil pattern and safer alternative.

prompts.label: When not to use regex
prompts.text:
List cases where regex is the wrong tool.

- Parsing HTML, XML, JSON, nested structures
- Reach for DOM parser, JSON.parse, dedicated libs
- Regex fine for logs and simple tokens
- Decision flowchart in bullets

Beginner guidance to avoid HTML regex meme.

prompts.label: JavaScript RegExp methods
prompts.text:
Survey JavaScript RegExp API for learners.

- .test(), .exec(), String.match, matchAll, replaceAll
- Literal /g flag global behavior
- lastIndex sticky global gotcha

Same pattern demonstrated three ways with outputs.

prompts.label: Python re module
prompts.text:
Teach Python re module essentials.

- re.search vs re.match vs re.fullmatch
- findall and finditer
- compile for reuse in loop
- raw strings r"pattern" habit

Script processing stdin lines matching pattern.

prompts.label: grep -E extended patterns
prompts.text:
Use grep -E for log filtering on command line.

- grep -E 'ERROR|WARN' app.log
- -i case insensitive, -n line numbers, -c count
- ripgrep rg as faster alternative mention
- Escape parens in basic vs extended

Five copy-paste recipes for devops beginners.

prompts.label: Extract JSON field loosely
prompts.text:
Extract field from JSON-like text without full parse (learning only).

- Pattern for "status":\s*"([^"]+)"
- Warn brittle vs JSON.parse
- When log line embeds json fragment

Show extract then recommend proper parser for prod.

prompts.label: Parse URL path segments
prompts.text:
Parse /api/users/123/posts/5 path segments with regex.

- Optional ^/api/users/(?<id>\d+)/posts/(?<postId>\d+)$
- Contrast URL class URL.pathname in JS
- When regex ok for routing framework internals vs hand-rolled

Provide match and named groups output.

prompts.label: Regex cheat sheet summary
prompts.text:
Produce a one-screen regex cheat sheet for beginners.

- Classes, anchors, quantifiers, groups, flags
- JS vs Python flag syntax differences table
- Top 5 mistakes list
- Links to regex101.com for testing habit

No novel pattern — recap only.
